newsitem.title: QATAR: GCC, EU to finish free trade accord talks by 1998.
newsitem.headline: GCC, EU to finish free trade accord talks by 1998.

text.p: Foreign ministers of Gulf Arab and European Union states, meeting in Doha on Monday, set a 1998 deadline to complete their negotiations for an inter-regional free trade agreement, officials said.

Officials of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) -- which groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and the United Arab Emirates -- met with EU officials in the Qatari capital for the one-day trade meeting.

"The joint council expressed its support for the planned, intensified programme for negotiations in 1997 which was intended to enable the two sides to complete the negotiations in 1998," said a communique issued after the seventh EU-GCC Ministerial Meeting.

"The joint council urged negotiators to continue their intensified efforts and reaffirmed its view that the free trade agreement...would not only be of mutual benefit but would also be fully compatible with the requirements of the World Trade Organisation," it said.

The GCC and its partners in the 15-nation EU have been discussing a free trade agreement for over a decade, but the accord has been delayed by Europe's insistence that the Gulf Arab states first align their widely divergent customs tariffs.

"The GCC side briefed the EU side on the progress in the finalisation of a unified GCC customs tariff as well as work on the wider aspects of a GCC customs union, which would be expedited so that it would be possible to be concluded by the time an EU-GCC trade agreement is ready for signature," the communique said.
Qatar's Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani told reporters after the meeting the work on unifying tariffs "would be completed by the year-end".
The communique also said the EU had pledged to support the WTO membership applications of Saudi Arabia and Oman, the only two GCC states not yet admitted to the organisation.

Sheikh Hamad applauded the EU move, saying: "The membership of these two states will have a positive impact on the multilateral trade system and will reinforce the role of the GCC as a regional bloc."
During the day's talks, the GCC and EU ministers also agreed to appoint a consultant to conduct a study and suggest measures to promote and protect investments in both regions.
